quests.instruction: On a clear night, the stars are easy to see. When thick clouds roll in, the stars become…
quests.hint: What can you see in the sky when clouds cover every gap?
quests.explanation: Visible means something can be seen. Invisible means it can’t be seen, even if it’s still there.
quests.funFact: Some stars are so far away that their light takes thousands of years to reach us.

quests.instruction: Water from the mountain stream was so clear that you could count the pebbles. After the storm, the same stream looked…
quests.hint: Heavy rain doesn’t only fall; it also carries something along.
quests.explanation: Clear water lets you see through it. Muddy water is cloudy and brown with soil.
quests.funFact: Rivers turn brown after heavy rain because they carry soil washed from the land.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “pale”? (the faint yellow of lemon ice cream vs. the deep color of melted chocolate)
quests.hint: Compare the color of a glass of milk with a cup of black coffee.
quests.explanation: A pale color is light and faint. A dark color is deep and strong.
quests.funFact: Adding white to a color makes a lighter version, called a tint.

quests.instruction: Last summer the poster was bright red. After a year in a sunny window, it looks…
quests.hint: What does strong sunlight slowly do to colors?
quests.explanation: Vivid colors are strong and bright. Faded ones have lost some of their brightness over time.
quests.funFact: Sunlight can break down dyes, which is why curtains and posters fade.

quests.instruction: A mouse squeaks with a thin, high-pitched sound. A big bear’s growl is much more…
quests.hint: Think of an animal with a very big chest and a very low growl.
quests.explanation: A high-pitched sound is thin and squeaky. A deep sound is low and rumbly.
quests.funFact: Big objects, like a large bell, tend to make lower sounds than small ones.

quests.instruction: The pyramids of Egypt are ancient. A solar-powered phone charger built last year is…
quests.hint: Which of the two could have been built thousands of years ago?
quests.explanation: Ancient means from a very long time ago. Modern means made or used now.
quests.funFact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is more than four thousand years old.

quests.instruction: Grandma’s glass vase breaks if you bump it. Her iron frying pan survives being dropped. The pan is…
quests.hint: Which one would you pack carefully for a long journey?
quests.explanation: Fragile things break easily. Sturdy things are strong enough to stand rough treatment.
quests.funFact: Glass breaks easily because it can’t bend much before it cracks.

quests.instruction: A table with four even legs stands steady. If one leg is shorter than the others, the table becomes…
quests.hint: Lean on one corner and notice what the table does.
quests.explanation: Steady means firm and not moving. Wobbly means shaking from side to side.
quests.funFact: Folding a small piece of paper under a short leg is an old trick for fixing a wobbly table.

quests.instruction: One chocolate egg is chocolate all the way through. Another is empty inside, which makes it…
quests.hint: What would you find if you cracked each egg open?
quests.explanation: Solid means filled all the way through. Hollow means there’s empty space inside.
quests.funFact: Bamboo stems are hollow, which keeps them light but strong.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “obvious”? (a bright red sign in the middle of the hall vs. a tiny note tucked behind a bookshelf)
quests.hint: Which one could you walk past a hundred times without noticing?
quests.explanation: Obvious things are easy to notice. Hidden things are tucked out of sight.
quests.funFact: Some insects look like leaves or sticks so that predators can’t find them.

quests.instruction: Chips and mango pickle are bursting with flavor. A bowl of boiled rice with nothing added is…
quests.hint: Food with no salt or spice would taste of very little.
quests.explanation: Tasty food has plenty of flavor. Bland food has very little.
quests.funFact: People have used salt and spices for thousands of years to add flavor to food.

quests.instruction: Peanut butter comes in two kinds: one full of nut bits you can bite, and one that’s smooth and soft. The first is crunchy. The second is…
quests.hint: Which kind would spread without any bumps?
quests.explanation: Crunchy foods have bits that crack in your mouth. Creamy foods are smooth all the way through.
quests.funFact: Peanuts aren’t true nuts; they grow underground and belong to the same family as peas and beans.

quests.instruction: The jasmine flowers smell lovely. The forgotten sports shoes at the bottom of the locker smell…
quests.hint: Which one would make you hold your nose?
quests.explanation: Fragrant means having a pleasant smell. Stinky means having a nasty one.
quests.funFact: Smells are strongly linked to memories, so a scent can remind you of a place instantly.

quests.instruction: A balloon pops with a bang, all at once. A sunrise takes a long time to brighten the sky. We say the sunrise is…
quests.hint: A flash or small steps? Decide that before you choose.
quests.explanation: Sudden means happening all at once. Gradual means happening bit by bit.
quests.funFact: The sky begins to brighten long before the sun appears; this early light is called dawn.

quests.instruction: Flamingos usually stand upright. Bats rest hanging from a roof with their heads pointing at the floor. They’re…
quests.hint: Which way is a bat’s head when it sleeps?
quests.explanation: Upright means standing with the top part up. Upside down means turned the other way around.
quests.funFact: A bat’s feet lock their grip, so they can hang without using much effort.

quests.instruction: Cars race along the highway. The cars waiting in the car park are…
quests.hint: What are the parked cars doing?
quests.explanation: Moving means changing position. Still means staying in the same place.
quests.funFact: Even when you’re sitting still, the Earth is carrying you around the Sun at about thirty kilometres every second.

quests.instruction: Mum scrubbed the white shirt until it was spotless. After lunch, a splash of curry left it…
quests.hint: Yellow sauce on a white shirt leaves a lasting mark.
quests.explanation: Spotless means without any marks. Stained means marked by something that didn’t wash out.
quests.funFact: Turmeric, used in many curries, can leave bright yellow stains.

quests.instruction: Rohit’s old sneakers had holes in the toes. The pair still sitting in the shop box is…
quests.hint: Which pair has never been walked in?
quests.explanation: Worn-out things have been used until they’re falling apart. Brand-new things have never been used.
quests.funFact: Sneakers got their name because rubber soles let people walk quietly, as if sneaking.

quests.instruction: A dust mite is so small you need a microscope to see it. A blue whale is…
quests.hint: Which animal needs the whole ocean?
quests.explanation: Tiny things are hard to see because they’re so small. Gigantic things are enormous.
quests.funFact: Dust mites are too small to see without a microscope.

quests.instruction: A rubber band bends and stretches easily. A wooden ruler snaps if you bend it too far. The ruler is…
quests.hint: Which of the two would you happily bend back and forth?
quests.explanation: Flexible things bend without breaking. Stiff things resist bending.
quests.funFact: Bamboo can bend a long way in strong wind without breaking.

quests.instruction: Anika’s raincoat kept her dry in the downpour. Her brother’s old boots let water seep in, so they were…
quests.hint: What reached his socks?
quests.explanation: Waterproof means water can’t get through. Leaky means water finds a way in.
quests.funFact: Duck feathers are coated with oil that helps water roll off.

quests.instruction: In winter, the oak tree stood with no leaves at all. In summer, its branches were…
quests.hint: What grows back on the branches in warmer months?
quests.explanation: A bare tree has no leaves on it. A leafy one is covered in them.
quests.funFact: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn to save energy through winter.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “furry”? (a rabbit with soft fur all over vs. a cat with almost no coat)
quests.hint: Think of an animal that would feel like skin, not fur, under your hand.
quests.explanation: Furry animals are covered in fur. Hairless ones have little or none.
quests.funFact: The Sphynx cat isn’t completely bald; it has a very fine layer of down.

quests.instruction: Sparrows can be seen in almost every town. A snow leopard is so shy and so few remain that spotting one is…
quests.hint: Which animal would you see on an ordinary walk to school?
quests.explanation: Common things are found all over the place. Rare things are seldom seen.
quests.funFact: Snow leopards live in the high mountains of Central and South Asia.

quests.instruction: Today is a normal Tuesday: just an ordinary day. Your birthday is a…
quests.hint: Which day do people sing to you?
quests.explanation: Ordinary days are like most others. Special ones stand out.
quests.funFact: Babies born on February 29 have their real birthday only once every four years.

quests.instruction: The plastic flowers in the shop window never need watering because they’re…
quests.hint: A real flower left without water wouldn’t last long, but a plastic one would.
quests.explanation: Real things are what they appear to be. Fake things only look like the real ones.
quests.funFact: Real leaves make food from sunlight, a process called photosynthesis. Plastic ones can’t.

quests.instruction: A river is a natural waterway. A channel dug by people to carry ships from sea to sea is…
quests.hint: Which waterway was planned and built by workers?
quests.explanation: Natural things form without people. Artificial things are made by people.
quests.funFact: The Suez Canal, an artificial waterway between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, opened in 1869.

quests.instruction: A hundred-piece puzzle with all hundred pieces is complete. If two pieces slip under the sofa, it’s…
quests.hint: What is the picture missing?
quests.explanation: Complete means nothing is missing. Incomplete means some parts are missing.
quests.funFact: A standard deck has 52 cards, so even one missing card makes it incomplete.

quests.instruction: After the monsoon, there’s plenty of grass for the cows. During a long drought, grass becomes…
quests.hint: Without rain, the pasture gets thin and patchy.
quests.explanation: Plenty means more than enough. Scarce means hardly any.
quests.funFact: Cacti store water in their thick stems to survive where water is scarce.

quests.instruction: Anyone can use the library or the playground. They’re public places. Your bedroom, where only family may come in, is…
quests.hint: Who is allowed in without asking?
quests.explanation: Public places belong to everyone. Private places are only for certain people.
quests.funFact: Public libraries lend books to everyone in a community, often for free.
